label: The parrot-fish is the only fish that chews the cud
claim: Of all fishes the scarus (parrot-fish) is the only one known to chew the cud like a quadruped.
quote: Of all fishes the so-called scarus, or parrot, wrasse, is the only one known to chew the cud like a quadruped.
scope: Sparisoma cretense (Mediterranean parrotfish) versus other fishes

label: Eels can live seven or eight years
claim: The eel lives in some cases for seven or eight years.
quote: The eel in some cases lives for seven or eight years.

label: Birds with crooked talons are all carnivorous and cannot swallow grain
claim: Birds with crooked talons are carnivorous without exception and cannot swallow grain or bread even if it is put into their bills.
quote: Of birds, such as have crooked talons are carnivorous without exception, and cannot swallow corn or bread-food even if it be put into their bills in tit-bits
scope: raptors: eagles, kites, hawks, buzzard, lammergeier, vultures, owls

label: Birds of prey almost never drink
claim: Birds as a rule drink very little, and birds of prey never drink at all apart from a very few that drink very rarely, such as the kestrel and the kite.
quote: In fact birds of prey never drink at all, excepting a very few, and these drink very rarely

label: Oviparous animals have a spongy, bloodless lung and drink little
claim: Scaly (tessellated) animals are spare drinkers, as are all animals with a spongy lung, and such a lung, poorly supplied with blood, is found in all oviparous animals.
quote: Tessellated animals are spare drinkers, as are also all such animals as have a spongy lung, and such a lung, scantily supplied with blood, is found in all oviparous animals.
scope: reptiles (lizards, snakes, tortoises) and other oviparous animals

label: Carnivores eat grass only when sick, to purge themselves
claim: Fierce, jag-toothed viviparous quadrupeds are all carnivorous and never eat grass except when sick, as dogs eat grass to make themselves vomit.
quote: These carnivorous animals never eat grass except when they are sick, just as dogs bring on a vomit by eating grass and thereby purge themselves.

label: A pig's carcass weighs five-sixths of its live weight
claim: A pig fattens faster for its size than any other animal, and after slaughter its flesh weighs five-sixths of its live weight, the hair, blood and the rest making up the other sixth.
quote: If a pig be weighed when living, you may calculate that after death its flesh will weigh five-sixths of that weight, and the hair, the blood, and the rest will weigh the other sixth.

label: Camels live about thirty years and occasionally to a hundred
claim: Camels live for about thirty years; some live much longer, and some have been known to reach a hundred.
quote: Camels live for about thirty years; in some exceptional cases they live much longer, and instances have been known of their living to the age of a hundred.

label: The bee is the only insect that always avoids rotten food
claim: The bee is the only insect that invariably avoids anything rotten and touches no food without a sweet juice.
quote: The bee is the only insect that invariably eschews whatever is rotten
scope: honey bee compared with other insects

label: Cranes migrate from Scythia to the marshes at the source of the Nile
claim: Cranes migrate from the steppes of Scythia to the marshlands south of Egypt where the Nile rises.
quote: for these birds migrate from the steppes of Scythia to the marshlands south of Egypt where the Nile has its source.

label: Migrants are fatter leaving cold for warm lands than on the return
claim: All animals are fatter when migrating from cold to warm regions than when migrating from warm to cold; the quail is fatter when it leaves in autumn than when it arrives in spring.
quote: All creatures are fatter in migrating from cold to heat than in migrating from heat to cold; thus the quail is fatter when he emigrates in autumn than when he arrives in spring.
scope: migratory animals, especially the common quail

label: Birds with crooked talons are short-necked, flat-tongued and mimics
claim: As a general rule all birds with crooked talons are short-necked, flat-tongued and given to mimicry, as is the parrot.
quote: As a general rule all birds with crooked talons are short-necked, flat-tongued, and disposed to mimicry.
scope: birds with hooked claws, including parrots and owls

label: The trichia leaves the Black Sea up the Danube into the Adriatic
claim: The trichia is caught entering but never leaving the Black Sea because it alone swims north into the Danube and, where the river divides, down into the Adriatic.
quote: The way of accounting for this phenomenon is that this fish, and this one only, swims northwards into the Danube, and then at the point of its bifurcation swims down southwards into the Adriatic.
scope: trichia (probably a sardine or shad) in the Black Sea, Danube and Adriatic

label: Animals hide away against extreme heat as well as extreme cold
claim: Animals go into concealment (dormancy) as a refuge against extreme heat as well as extreme cold; shellfish all do so, snails in winter and the purple murex and scallop in the hottest season.
quote: animals go into concealment by way of refuge against extreme heat, as well as against extreme cold.
scope: animals generally; land snails, purple murex, scallop

label: Snakes and lizards hide for four months in winter and eat nothing
claim: Scaly animals such as the serpent, lizard, gecko and river crocodile go into hiding for four months in the depth of winter and eat nothing during that time.
quote: all of which go into hiding for four months in the depth of winter, and during that time eat nothing.

label: Many birds hide in winter rather than migrate, including swallows
claim: Many birds do not migrate to warmer countries but hide where they are in winter; swallows have often been found in holes without feathers, and the kite, stork, turtle-dove, lark and others go into hiding.
quote: A great number of birds also go into hiding; they do not all migrate, as is generally supposed, to warmer countries.
scope: swallow, kite, stork, owzel, turtle-dove, lark, thrush, starling, owl

label: The she-bear gives birth during winter concealment and emerges in spring
claim: The she-bear gives birth while in winter concealment and stays hidden until she brings the cubs out in spring, about three months after the winter solstice; bears eat nothing while hidden.
quote: The female brings forth her young at this time, and remains in concealment until it is time to bring the cubs out; and she brings them out in spring, about three months after the winter solstice.

label: Crustaceans moult not once but repeatedly
claim: Crabs, crawfish and lobsters slough their shells, becoming soft all over, and they do so not once for all but over and over again.
quote: These animals also do not cast their skins once and for all, but over and over again.

label: Fishes have no pestilential diseases like those of man and livestock
claim: No pestilential (epidemic) disease is known to attack fishes as such diseases attack man, horses and oxen, although individual fishes do appear to fall sick.
quote: We know of no pestilential malady attacking fishes, such as those which attack man, and horses and oxen among the quadrupedal vivipara

label: The purple murex dies within a day of tasting fresh water
claim: Shellfish generally benefit from rain, but the purple murex is an exception: placed near a river mouth, it dies within a day of tasting fresh water.
quote: if it be placed on a shore near to where a river discharges, it will die within a day after tasting the fresh water.

label: The pig is the only animal known to get measles
claim: The pig is the only animal known to suffer from 'measles' (pimples in the flesh, seen especially under the tongue), and pigs never get it while still sucklings.
quote: The pig is the only animal known to be subject to measles.
scope: pigs; 'measles' corresponds to cysticercosis (Taenia solium cysts)

label: Rabies passes to every animal bitten by a mad dog except man
claim: Rabies drives dogs mad and is fatal to them, and any animal bitten by a rabid dog catches it and dies, with the exception of man.
quote: ary animal whatever, excepting man, will take the disease if bitten by a dog so afflicted; the disease is fatal to the dog itself, and to any animal it may bite, man excepted.

label: The ass tolerates cold least and is absent from Scythia
claim: Of all animals of its kind the ass is least able to endure extreme cold, which is why it is not found on the shores of the Black Sea or in Scythia.
quote: Of all animals on its of its kind it is the least capable of enduring extreme cold, which circumstance will account for the fact that the animal is not found on the shores of the Euxine, nor in Scythia.
scope: donkey compared with horse and mule

label: All insects die when smeared with oil
claim: All insects without exception die if smeared with oil, and die faster if the head is smeared and they are laid in the sun.
quote: All insects, without exception, die if they be smeared over with oil; and they die all the more rapidly if you smear their head with the oil and lay them out in the sun.

label: The leopard is absent from Europe while lions live in part of Greece
claim: Lions are more numerous in Libya and in the part of Europe between the Achelous and the Nessus rivers; the leopard is more abundant in Asia Minor and is not found in Europe at all.
quote: lions are more numerous in Libya, and in that district of Europe that lies between the Achelous and the Nessus; the leopard is more abundant in Asia Minor, and is not found in Europe at all.
scope: lion and leopard in the ancient Mediterranean

label: Different species breed together if similar in size and gestation length
claim: In Libya animals of different species meet at watering places and pair, and such pairs often breed if they are nearly the same size and have gestation periods of the same length.
quote: such pairs will often breed if they be nearly of the same size and have periods of gestation of the same length.

label: Wolves and dogs interbreed, and the Laconian hound is a fox–dog cross
claim: Animals of different kinds produce hybrids: in Cyrene the wolf and the bitch couple and breed, and the Laconian hound is a cross between the fox and the dog.
quote: Elsewhere also bastard-animals are born to heterogeneous pairs; thus in Cyrene the wolf and the bitch will couple and breed; and the Laconian hound is a cross between the fox and the dog.

label: A scaly fish's age can be told from the size and hardness of its scales
claim: The age of a scaly fish can be told from the size and hardness of its scales.
quote: The age of a scaly fish may be told by the size and the hardness of its scales.

label: Females are less spirited than males, except in the bear and leopard
claim: In all animals with separate sexes the female is less spirited (less courageous) than the male, except in the bear and the leopard, where the female is the more courageous.
quote: In all cases, excepting those of the bear and leopard, the female is less spirited than the male; in regard to the two exceptional cases, the superiority in courage rests with the female.
scope: animals with separate sexes, with the bear and leopard as exceptions

label: Animals sharing a locality or food are enemies
claim: Animals that live in the same localities or feed on the same food are enemies, and when food runs short animals of the same kind fight one another.
quote: There is enmity between such animals as dwell in the same localities or subsist on the food. If the means of subsistence run short, creatures of like kind will fight together.
scope: animals in general, intra- and interspecific

label: With unlimited food, wild animals would be tame to man and each other
claim: If there were no shortage of food, animals that are now wild or afraid of man would become tame towards man and peaceable towards one another, as fed animals in Egypt show.
quote: One may go so far as to say that if there were no lack or stint of food, then those animals that are now afraid of man or are wild by nature would be tame and familiar with him, and in like manner with one another.
scope: wild animals generally, including predators such as crocodiles

label: Stag antler points increase yearly until about six years old
claim: Stags grow no horns in their first year, unbranched spikes in their second, two-pointed antlers in the third and three-pointed in the fourth, increasing in complexity until about six years old, after which antlers no longer indicate age.
quote: In the third year the antlers are bifurcate; in the fourth year they grow trifurcate; and so they go on increasing in complexity until the creature is six years old: after this they grow their horns without any specific differentiation, so that you cannot by observation of them tell the animal's age.

label: Hinds swallow the afterbirth immediately after giving birth
claim: After giving birth, the hind (female deer) at once swallows the afterbirth, catching it before it falls to the ground.
quote: The hinds after parturition at once swallow the afterbirth, and it is impossible to secure it, for the hind catches it before it falls to the ground

label: Sick animals treat themselves, e.g. dogs eat grass to vomit
claim: Many quadrupeds treat their own ailments: dogs, when ill, eat a kind of grass that makes them vomit.
quote: Many other quadrupeds help themselves in clever ways. Wild goats in Crete are said, when wounded by arrows, to go in search of dittany, which is supposed to have the property of ejecting arrows in the body. Dogs, when they are ill, eat some kind of grass and produce vomiting.
scope: quadrupeds, with dogs as the stated case

label: The trochilus cleans the crocodile's teeth
claim: When the crocodile gapes, a small bird, the trochilus, enters its mouth and cleans its teeth, feeding itself thereby, and the crocodile does not harm it.
quote: When the crocodile yawns, the trochilus flies into his mouth and cleans his teeth. The trochilus gets his food thereby, and the crocodile gets ease and comfort; it makes no attempt to injure its little friend
scope: Nile crocodile and the trochilus (a small Egyptian bird)

label: Pigeons pair for life
claim: Pigeons pair with the same mate until one of the pair dies, though occasionally a female mates with a bird other than her mate.
quote: In pairing the same male and the same female keep together; and the union is only broken by the death of one of the two parties.
scope: pigeons and doves (tame pigeon, ring-dove, turtle-dove)

label: Heavy-bodied birds like quails and partridges build no nests
claim: Heavy-bodied birds such as quails and partridges build no nests but lay in a scraped hollow on level ground, since nest building would be of no use to birds that cannot fly well.
quote: Birds of a heavy build, such as quails, partridges, and the like, build no nests; indeed, where they are incapable of flight, it would be of no use if they could do so.
scope: heavy-bodied ground birds (quails, partridges and similar galliforms)

label: Partridge hens feign lameness to lure intruders from the brood
claim: When a man comes upon a partridge brood, the hen rolls in front of him pretending to be lame, drawing him away until the young have escaped, then returns and calls them back.
quote: When a man comes by chance upon a young brood, and tries to catch them, the hen-bird rolls in front of the hunter, pretending to be lame: the man every moment thinks he is on the point of catching her, and so she draws him on and on, until every one of her brood has had time to escape

label: Web-footed birds all live near water
claim: All web-footed birds live near the sea, rivers or pools, because they resort to places suited to their structure.
quote: Web-footed birds without exception live near the sea or rivers or pools, as they naturally resort to places adapted to their structure.
scope: web-footed birds (ducks, geese, swans, gulls and similar)

label: Swans sing chiefly as they approach death
claim: Swans are musical and sing chiefly at the approach of death, flying out to sea at that time.
quote: They are musical, and sing chiefly at the approach of death; at this time they fly out to sea, and men, when sailing past the coast of Libya, have fallen in with many of them out at sea singing in mournful strains

label: The cuckoo lays a single egg in another bird's nest and does not hatch it
claim: The cuckoo builds no nest, lays only one egg in the nest of another bird, and leaves the foster mother to hatch and rear it.
quote: it lays only one egg and does not hatch it itself, but the mother-bird in whose nest it has deposited it hatches and rears it
scope: common cuckoo (Cuculus canorus) and its hosts (ring-dove, lark, hypolais, green linnet)

label: Cuckoos lay in others' nests because of their own cowardice
claim: The cuckoo places its young in another bird's nest because it is the most cowardly of birds and could not defend its young in an emergency.
quote: The cuckoo shows great sagacity in the disposal of its progeny; the fact is, the mother cuckoo is quite conscious of her own cowardice and of the fact that she could never help her young one in an emergency

label: A pair of eagles needs a large territory and drives other birds away
claim: A pair of eagles needs an extensive area to maintain itself, so it expels its fledged young from the neighbourhood and does not allow other birds to settle nearby.
quote: The fact is that a pair of eagles demands an extensive space for its maintenance, and consequently cannot allow other birds to quarter themselves in close neighbourhood.

label: The sea-eagle makes its young stare at the sun and kills those that cannot
claim: Before its young are fledged the sea-eagle makes them stare at the sun, beats any that refuse, and kills one whose eyes water.
quote: the sea-eagle is very keen-sighted, and before its young are fledged tries to make them stare at the sun, and beats the one that refuses to do so, and twists him back in the sun's direction; and if one of them gets watery eyes in the process, it kills him, and rears the other.

label: The fishing-frog lures prey with filaments in front of its eyes
claim: The fishing-frog (angler) has long thin filaments with rounded tips in front of its eyes which it raises as bait while hidden in sand and mud, drawing small fish that touch them into its mouth.
quote: The fishing-frog has a set of filaments that project in front of its eyes; they are long and thin like hairs, and are round at the tips; they lie on either side, and are used as baits.

label: The torpedo stuns its prey with a shock from its body
claim: The torpedo (electric ray) catches its prey by numbing it with a shock residing in its body, and can numb humans too.
quote: The torpedo narcotizes the creatures that it wants to catch, overpowering them by the power of shock that is resident in its body, and feeds upon them

label: The male sheat-fish guards the spawn for forty to fifty days
claim: In the sheat-fish the female leaves after spawning while the male guards the spawn and fry, driving off small fish, for forty or fifty days until the young can escape on their own.
quote: contenting himself with keeping off all other little fishes that might steal the spawn or fry, and this he does for forty or fifty days, until the young are sufficiently grown to make away from the other fishes for themselves.

label: All fish are carnivorous except a few, and carnivorous fish wander most
claim: All fish are carnivorous except a few such as the grey mullet, the saupe, the red mullet and the chalcis, and the carnivorous fish wander most.
quote: Carnivorous fish wander most; and all fish are carnivorous with the exception of a few, such as the mullet, the saupe, the red mullet, and the chalcis.

label: Only the sepia uses its ink for concealment; octopus and squid ink from fear
claim: Among cephalopods the sepia (cuttlefish) alone discharges its ink for concealment as well as from fear, while the octopus and calamary (squid) discharge it only from fear.
quote: Of molluscs the sepia is the most cunning, and is the only species that employs its dark liquid for the sake of concealment as well as from fear: the octopus and calamary make the discharge solely from fear.

label: The octopus changes colour to match nearby stones
claim: The octopus hunts by changing its colour to match the adjacent stones, and does so also when alarmed.
quote: It seeks its prey by so changing its colour as to render it like the colour of the stones adjacent to it; it does so also when alarmed.

label: The octopus as a rule does not live beyond one year
claim: The octopus as a rule does not live a full year, and after spawning the female in particular becomes weak, stupid and wastes away.
quote: The octopus as a rule does not live the year out.

label: The argonaut uses its web as a sail and arms as oars
claim: The nautilus (argonaut) rises to the surface and, when a breeze blows, uses a thin web between its arms as a sail and lets down some arms as rudder-oars.
quote: It uses this structure, when a breeze is blowing, for a sail, and lets down some of its feelers alongside as rudder-oars.

label: Spiders spin from the surface of the body, not from an excretion
claim: Spiders can spin from birth, and their thread comes off the body like bark rather than from inside as a superfluity or excretion, contrary to Democritus.
quote: Spiders can spin webs from the time of their birth, not from their interior as a superfluity or excretion, as Democritus avers, but off their body as a kind of tree-bark

label: On each trip a bee visits flowers of only one kind
claim: On each foraging trip a bee goes from flower to flower of one kind only and does not visit another kind until it has returned to the hive.
quote: On each expedition the bee does not fly from a flower of one kind to a flower of another, but flies from one violet, say, to another violet, and never meddles with another flower until it has got back to the hive

label: Bees kill most of their kings to prevent the hive splitting
claim: Worker bees kill most of their kings, especially inferior ones, to prevent a multiplicity of kings from splitting the hive, and destroy royal cells when no swarm is intended.
quote: These bees also kill without mercy most of their kings, and especially kings of the inferior sort; and this they do for fear a multiplicity of kings should lead to a dismemberment of the hive.

label: A bee that stings dies because it loses its gut with the sting
claim: A bee that stings dies because it cannot withdraw its sting without tearing out its intestines; once it loses its sting it must die.
quote: Bees that sting die from their inability to extract the sting without at the same time extracting their intestines.

label: Older bees work indoors, younger bees forage outside
claim: Older bees do the work inside the hive and are rough and hairy from staying indoors, while young bees do the carrying outside and are comparatively smooth.
quote: The elder bees do the indoor work, and are rough and hairy from staying indoors; the young bees do the outer carrying, and are comparatively smooth.

label: Bees carry a stone as ballast in high wind
claim: In a high wind bees carry a stone as ballast to steady their flight.
quote: In a high wind they carry a stone by way of ballast to steady them.

label: Worker wasps all die in winter; only the mother-wasps overwinter
claim: Worker wasps do not survive into a second year but all die as winter comes on, while the larger mother-wasps survive the winter in holes underground.
quote: The workers do not live over into a second year, but all die when winter comes on; and this can be proved, for at the commencement of winter the workers become drowsy, and about the time of the winter solstice they are never seen at all.

label: Lions attack humans when old and their teeth are diseased
claim: Lions invade cattle-folds and attack humans when old age and diseased teeth prevent them from catching their usual prey.
quote: They invade the cattle-folds and attack human beings when they are grown old and so by reason of old age and the diseased condition of their teeth are unable to pursue their wonted prey.

label: The elephant breathes through its trunk to cross water
claim: The elephant can make its way through water as long as the tip of its trunk is above the surface, because it breathes through its trunk.
quote: he can make his way through water, as long as the tip of his trunk can be above the surface, for he blows with his trunk and breathes through it.

label: Hens that beat a cock become cock-like, even growing spurs
claim: Hens that have beaten the cock in a fight crow like a cock, try to tread him, raise a crest and tail-feathers, and sometimes grow small spurs.
quote: Hens, for instance, when they have beaten the cock in a fight, will crow like the cock and endeavour to tread him; the crest rises up on their head and the tail-feathers on the rump, so that it becomes difficult to recognize that they are hens; in some cases there is a growth of small spurs.

label: Castrated cocks lose their crest colour, crowing and sexual drive
claim: A full-grown cock castrated by cauterizing the rump loses the colour of its crest, stops crowing and loses sexual desire; if castrated young, it never develops these male traits.
quote: If you burn this twice or thrice with hot irons, then, if the bird be full-grown, his crest grows sallow, he ceases to crow, and foregoes sexual passion; but if you cauterize the bird when young, none of these male attributes propensities will come to him as he grows up.

label: Boys castrated before puberty keep a high voice; eunuchs never go bald
claim: Men castrated in boyhood never grow the later hair and keep a high-pitched voice, and a eunuch never goes bald.
quote: if you mutilate them in boyhood, the later-growing hair never comes, and the voice never changes but remains high-pitched

label: Stags castrated before growing horns never grow them
claim: Stags castrated before they have horns never grow horns, and stags castrated when they have horns keep them unchanged in size and do not shed them.
quote: If stags be mutilated, when, by reason of their age, they have as yet no horns, they never grow horns at all; if they be mutilated when they have horns, the horns remain unchanged in size, and the animal does not lose them.

label: Animals lacking upper teeth are the ones that ruminate
claim: The animals that ruminate are those lacking upper (front) teeth, such as cattle, sheep and goats, though a few with teeth in both jaws also ruminate.
quote: It is the animals that lack the upper teeth that ruminate, such as kine, sheep, and goats.

label: Many birds change plumage colour and song with the seasons
claim: Many birds change the colour of their plumage and their song with the season; for example, the blackbird turns yellow instead of black and its song changes.
quote: A considerable number of birds change according to season the colour of their plumage and their note; as, for instance, the owsel becomes yellow instead of black, and its note gets altered
scope: birds generally; blackbird (Turdus merula), thrush, nightingale

label: The redbreast and the redstart are one bird in two seasonal forms
claim: The robin (a winter bird) and the redstart (a summer bird) change into one another and differ only in plumage colour; likewise the beccafico and the blackcap.
quote: The erithacus (or redbreast) and the so-called redstart change into one another; the former is a winter bird, the latter a summer one, and the difference between them is practically limited to the coloration of their plumage.
scope: European robin (Erithacus rubecula) and common redstart (Phoenicurus phoenicurus); garden warbler and blackcap

label: Ground birds dust-bathe; waterside birds water-bathe
claim: Birds that do not fly but live on the ground take dust-baths, waterside birds and some straight-taloned birds take water-baths, and most crooked-taloned birds take neither.
quote: Birds that do not fly but keep on the ground take the dust-bath, as for instance the hen, the partridge, the francolin, the crested lark, the pheasant; some of the straight-taloned birds, and such as live on the banks of a river, in marshes, or by the sea, take a water-bath
scope: birds: galliforms and larks; waterside birds; raptors

label: The final cause comes before the motor cause in explaining nature
claim: Of the causes at work in the generation of natural things, the final cause (the end or purpose) is prior to the motor cause, in nature as in art.
quote: Plainly, however, that cause is the first which we call the final one. For this is the Reason, and the Reason forms the starting-point, alike in the works of art and in works of nature.
scope: all works of nature, including animals and their parts

label: The vertebrae are not formed by accidental breaking of the foetal backbone
claim: The division of the backbone into vertebrae is not, as Empedocles held, the result of the backbone being broken by the contorted position of the foetus in the womb, nor are animal characters in general mere incidents of development.
quote: Empedocles, then, was in error when he said that many of the characters presented by animals were merely the results of incidental occurrences during their development; for instance, that the backbone was divided as it is into vertebrae, because it happened to be broken owing to the contorted position of the foetus in the womb.

label: Like begets like: the parent's characters determine the offspring's
claim: Man is generated from man, and it is the possession of certain characters by the parent that determines the development of like characters in the offspring.
quote: For man is generated from man; and thus it is the possession of certain characters by the parent that determines the development of like characters in the child.
scope: all animals that are generated from parents, with man as the example

label: Only man has intellect, though other animals move themselves
claim: Other animals besides man have the power of locomotion, but none but man has intellect.
quote: I say not the intellectual part; for other animals than man have the power of locomotion, but in none but him is there intellect.
scope: all animals, man contrasted with the rest

label: Respiration is driven by an alternation of heat and cooling
claim: Breathing exists for the alternate discharge and re-entry of heat, and the alternation of heating and cooling in the body necessarily produces the alternate intake and discharge of outer air.
quote: For the alternate discharge and re-entrance of heat and the inflow of air are necessary if we are to live. Here we have at once a necessity in the former of the two senses. But the alternation of heat and refrigeration produces of necessity an alternate admission and discharge of the outer air, and this is a necessity of the second kind.

label: Some ants fly and others do not
claim: Among ants some fly and others do not, so Flying versus Walking cannot be used to divide animal kinds.
quote: For some groups, Ants for instance, fall under both divisions, some ants flying while others do not.
